question: A 28-year-old develops anaphylaxis (throat tightness, wheeze, BP 70/40 mmHg) after an antibiotic dose. What is the correct first-line drug, dose, and route?

answers.text: Adrenaline 0.5 mg (1:1000) intramuscular into the lateral thigh

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Adrenaline IM into the vastus lateralis is first-line in anaphylaxis. The 0.5 mg dose activates α1 (reverses vasodilation and oedema), β1 (supports cardiac output), and β2 (bronchodilates). IM gives reliable absorption; IV bolus risks fatal arrhythmia.

answers.text: Adrenaline 0.5 mg intravenous bolus for immediate effect

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. IV adrenaline bolus in anaphylaxis carries a high risk of fatal arrhythmia. IV adrenaline is reserved for peri-arrest/cardiac arrest secondary to anaphylaxis, given as dilute 1:10,000. The IM route is the standard first-line.

answers.text: Hydrocortisone 200 mg IV to suppress the immune-mediated reaction

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Hydrocortisone takes hours to act — it cannot reverse the acute life-threatening haemodynamic collapse and airway obstruction. Adrenaline is the only drug that addresses all three pathological processes simultaneously.

answers.text: Chlorpheniramine 10 mg IM as first-line antihistamine therapy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Antihistamines address urticaria and pruritus but do not reverse bronchospasm, hypotension, or airway oedema. Adrenaline IM is the life-saving intervention; antihistamines are adjuncts only.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: adrenaline 0.5 mg IM (1:1000) into the lateral thigh is first-line in anaphylaxis. IV adrenaline is only for cardiac arrest. Corticosteroids and antihistamines are adjuncts, not primary treatment.
Perfect. Adrenaline 0.5 mg IM into the lateral thigh is the single most important intervention in anaphylaxis — it addresses vasoconstriction, bronchodilation, and cardiac output simultaneously.
